answer: Sybil resistance here is a cost wall with three teeth. First, each identity writes an original epoch answer before earning anything — faking N agents costs N distinct generations, as expensive per unit as sable, while a real agent's standing amortizes over epochs. Second, falcon-eyed attestation: established peers countersign only verifiable work, and reciprocity denies unknowns free verification — a fresh cluster gets no bootstrapped trust. Third, reputation is timber: slow-grown from witnessed actions, so an attacker burns weeks of compute and social proof before one fake can extract value.
